vocabulary.meaning_en: a move to a higher position in your company
vocabulary.example: She got a promotion after two years.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to show official thanks for someone's work
vocabulary.example: This award recognises your hard work.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something good that you did with effort
vocabulary.example: Winning the contract was a great achievement.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a very rare and very good chance
vocabulary.example: Working in the head office is the opportunity of a lifetime.

vocabulary.meaning_en: your most trusted helper at work
vocabulary.example: She is the director's right-hand woman.

vocabulary.meaning_en: that people believe is honest and reliable
vocabulary.example: He is a trusted member of staff.

vocabulary.meaning_en: extremely useful; so useful you cannot measure its value
vocabulary.example: Your help has been invaluable.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say yes to an offer
vocabulary.example: I'd be delighted to accept the job.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very pleased
vocabulary.example: I'm delighted to hear the news.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the rules and details of an agreement, such as pay and hours
vocabulary.example: Could we discuss the terms and conditions of the contract?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to think carefully about something before deciding
vocabulary.example: Could I have some time to consider your offer?

vocabulary.meaning_en: something that someone says they will give you, e.g. a job
vocabulary.example: Thank you for your offer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: nice things someone says about you
vocabulary.example: Thank you for your kind words.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to accept a job or responsibility
vocabulary.example: I'm not sure I can take on that much responsibility.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having skill and knowledge from doing something for a long time
vocabulary.example: We need an experienced manager.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to be good enough to do a job
vocabulary.example: I'm sure you're up to the job.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take the place of someone or something
vocabulary.example: Anna will replace Paul as manager.

vocabulary.meaning_en: announced and approved by people in authority
vocabulary.example: Don't tell anyone until it's official.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not willing to talk about something
vocabulary.example: He stayed tight-lipped about the new project.

vocabulary.meaning_en: exactly the kind of thing you like or are good at
vocabulary.example: A job in design is right up your street.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a difficult choice between two things
vocabulary.example: Taking the job or staying in my city - what a dilemma!

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) very easy
vocabulary.example: This task is easy peasy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you do often, almost without thinking
vocabulary.example: I have a habit of changing my mind.

fine_lines.title: valuable vs invaluable
fine_lines.explanation_ar: قد يظن المتعلم أن invaluable عكس valuable، لكنها في الحقيقة أقوى منها: invaluable تعني «بالغ الأهمية، لا يقدّر بثمن». أما عكس valuable فهو worthless أو of little value.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Invaluable is NOT the opposite of valuable. It is stronger: extremely useful. The opposite of valuable is worthless.

examples.sentence: Your advice has been invaluable to the team.

fine_lines.title: experience vs experienced
fine_lines.explanation_ar: experience اسم معناه «الخبرة» (I have experience). experienced صفة معناها «ذو خبرة» تصف الشخص (an experienced manager).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Experience is a noun (I have five years' experience). Experienced is an adjective that describes a person (an experienced manager).

examples.sentence: Tom is more experienced than me.

fine_lines.title: accept vs except
fine_lines.explanation_ar: النطق متقارب لكن المعنى مختلف: accept فعل بمعنى «يقبل»، وexcept حرف بمعنى «ما عدا».
fine_lines.explanation_en: They sound similar but are different: accept is a verb (say yes to); except means 'but not'.

examples.sentence: I'd be delighted to accept the offer.
Everyone came to the meeting except Tom.

expressions.phrase: This promotion recognises your achievements at the company.
expressions.meaning_ar: هذه الترقية تقدير لإنجازاتك في الشركة.
expressions.meaning_en: You get this promotion because of your good work.
expressions.example: This promotion recognises your achievements over the last three years.

expressions.phrase: It's an opportunity of a lifetime.
expressions.meaning_en: This is a very rare, very good chance.
expressions.example: Working in our Tokyo office is an opportunity of a lifetime.

expressions.phrase: You would be my right-hand man / woman.
expressions.meaning_en: You would be my most trusted helper.
expressions.example: If you take the job, you would be my right-hand woman.

expressions.phrase: I'd be delighted to accept. Thank you.
expressions.meaning_ar: يسعدني كثيرًا أن أقبل. شكرًا لك.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to say yes to an offer.
expressions.example: Thank you for the offer. I'd be delighted to accept.

expressions.meaning_en: A polite question about the start date.
expressions.example: That sounds wonderful. When would I start?

expressions.phrase: Could we discuss the terms and conditions of the new job?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكننا مناقشة شروط الوظيفة الجديدة وأحكامها؟
expressions.meaning_en: Can we talk about pay, hours and other details?
expressions.example: Before I say yes, could we discuss the terms and conditions of the new job?

expressions.phrase: Thank you for your kind words, but could I have some time to consider your offer?
expressions.meaning_ar: شكرًا على كلماتك اللطيفة، لكن هل يمكنني الحصول على بعض الوقت لدراسة عرضك؟
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to ask for time before deciding.
expressions.example: Thank you for your kind words, but could I have some time to consider your offer?

expressions.phrase: This news has come as a bit of a shock.
expressions.meaning_ar: هذا الخبر كان مفاجئًا بعض الشيء.
expressions.meaning_en: I did not expect this news.
expressions.example: This news has come as a bit of a shock. I need to think.

grammar.title: would for polite answers and questions about an offer
grammar.explanation_ar: عند الحديث عن عرض لم نقبله بعد نستخدم would لأنه أمر افتراضي ومهذب: I'd (= I would) be delighted to accept، When would I start?، You would be my right-hand man.
grammar.explanation_en: When we talk about an offer that is not final yet, we use 'would' - it is polite and hypothetical: I'd be delighted to accept. When would I start? You would be my right-hand man.
examples: I'd be delighted to join your team.

grammar.title: Asking for time: Could I have some time to + verb?
grammar.explanation_ar: إذا احتجت وقتًا للتفكير اطلب ذلك بأدب: Could I have some time to consider/think about…? ويمكن أن تبدأ بشكر: Thank you for your kind words, but…
grammar.explanation_en: If you need time to decide, ask politely: Could I have some time to consider / think about...? You can start with thanks: Thank you for your kind words, but...
examples: Could I have some time to think about it?
Could I have a few days to consider your offer?
Thank you, but could I have until Monday to decide?

questions.question: Which is the best way to accept a job offer politely?
choices: I'd be delighted to accept. Thank you.
questions.explanation_ar: I'd be delighted to accept عبارة مهذبة للقبول.
questions.explanation_en: 'I'd be delighted to accept' is polite.

questions.question: 'It's an opportunity of a lifetime' means…
choices: it's a very rare, very good chance
questions.explanation_ar: فرصة العمر أي فرصة نادرة جدًّا وجيدة.
questions.explanation_en: It is a very rare and good chance.

questions.question: A 'right-hand man' is…
choices: a man who writes with his right hand
a person who leaves the company
questions.explanation_ar: right-hand man هو المساعد الأكثر ثقة.
questions.explanation_en: It means your most trusted assistant.

questions.question: Could we discuss the ___ of the new job?
questions.explanation_ar: terms and conditions هي الشروط مثل الراتب وساعات العمل.
questions.explanation_en: Terms and conditions = pay, hours and other details.

questions.question: 'Your help has been invaluable' means your help has been…
questions.explanation_ar: invaluable تعني بالغ الأهمية وليست عكس valuable.

questions.question: Anna needs time to think. What should she say?
choices: Could I have some time to consider your offer?
questions.explanation_ar: لطلب وقت للتفكير نقول Could I have some time to consider…
questions.explanation_en: To ask for time: 'Could I have some time to consider your offer?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: He is more experience than me.
He is more experienced than me.
questions.explanation_en: 'Experienced' is the adjective describing a person.

questions.question: Tom says he will be 'tight-lipped'. He means he will…
questions.explanation_en: Tight-lipped means he won't say anything.

questions.question: Paul's new job as Head Taster is 'right up his street'. This means…
questions.explanation_ar: right up your street أي يناسبك تمامًا.
questions.explanation_en: It means it's exactly the kind of thing he likes.
